owner_synthesis.what_this_is: New Roads Therapeutic Recovery Community is an operating, nonprofit-run residential recovery program in the Victoria area. This dossier connects a named provincial funding commitment to its recipient, continuing service evidence and a later women’s-program expansion.
what_we_learned: The Province named New Roads and announced $4.39 million over three years to support an estimated 330 participants.
Our Place Society is the named operator and recipient relationship; Island Health currently lists the program within its treatment-and-recovery directory.
A separate 20-bed women’s facility opened in March 2025, demonstrating a later expansion of the New Roads model.
The funding-to-service path reaches service level, but Miller still needs an owner decision about whether the men’s and women’s programs are one resource or related resources.
owner_synthesis.why_it_matters: This is the clearest canonical example of public money moving from a named government announcement to a named operator and an observable service, while preserving a remaining resource-identity decision.
what_remains_unclear: How should the men’s and women’s New Roads programs map to canonical Miller resource records?
Is there a public post-award report comparing actual participation with the estimated 330 people over three years?
owner_synthesis.recommended_next_move: Send the two-program identity question through normal Miller owner review before considering either resource record or backstory for publication.

unresolved_questions.rationale: Operation is established, but current assembled sources do not measure performance against the announced participation estimate.

foi_candidates.exact_missing_information: Program-level participant counts and any final reporting tied to the $4.39-million New Roads contribution.
foi_candidates.why_it_matters: It would distinguish an announced participation estimate from documented delivery without seeking individual-level information.
foi_candidates.suggested_record_category: final grant results, aggregate program reporting or contribution-agreement performance summary

edges.neutral_summary: The Province announced a named $4.39-million, three-year funding commitment for New Roads.
The official announcement associates the funding with the Our Place Society-operated New Roads program.
The operator and health-authority pages identify New Roads as a current service.
Current service evidence supports a service-level funding-to-operation path; it does not provide detailed expenditure attribution.
An official opening notice documents the later 20-bed women’s facility as an expansion of the New Roads model.

owner_assessment.owner_review_reason: The evidence chain is strong, but resource identity and program granularity require a normal Miller editorial decision.
owner_assessment.recommended_next_action: Resolve the one-versus-two-resource representation and then test the dossier projection against that private candidate mapping.

quality_assessment.notice: Research completeness only; this is not a moral, effectiveness, compliance, or reputational score.

limitations: The dossier establishes a named funding-to-operation path but does not audit expenditure, evaluate effectiveness or allocate costs among program components. It also leaves the final Miller resource granularity to owner review.
